sentences.en: In today's episode, we are diving into the psychology of death anxiety.

sentences.en: What it is, how often it crops up, and what happens when it starts to interfere with daily life.

sentences.en: Whether you've ever had a passing fear of dying or you find yourself avoiding the topic completely, you're not alone.
sentences.zh: 无论你是否曾对死亡产生过一闪而过的恐惧，还是发现自己完全在逃避这个话题，你都不是一个人。

sentences.zh: 很高兴你能来。

sentences.zh: 你好，玛丽安和大家。

sentences.en: Thank you for being here.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你来到这里。

sentences.en: So we are thinking today about kind of where you are right now, which is that you are an end-stage trainee clinical psychologist who yesterday completed her viva and passed.
sentences.zh: 所以我们今天想探讨的是你目前所处的阶段，也就是你是一名即将毕业的临床心理学实习生，昨天刚完成毕业论文答辩并通过了。

sentences.en: Congratulations.
sentences.zh: 恭喜你。

sentences.en: And we are thinking about specifically your research today, which is on death anxiety.
sentences.zh: 我们今天特别想探讨你的研究，主题是关于死亡焦虑。

sentences.en: Is that right?
sentences.zh: 是这样吗？

sentences.en: Yes, that's right.
sentences.zh: 是的，正是如此。

sentences.en: Amazing.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: So what is death anxiety?
sentences.zh: 那么，什么是死亡焦虑？

sentences.en: I mean, death anxiety really is the fear or the unease about our own death or the dying process.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，死亡焦虑实际上是对我们自己的死亡或垂死过程的恐惧或不安。

sentences.en: And this can show up as worry of losing control or, you know, the unknown, because we don't,
sentences.zh: 这表现为对失去控制的担忧，或者你知道的，对未知的恐惧，因为我们不知道，

sentences.en: most of us don't know what's going to happen after we pass and kind of what happens after life.
sentences.zh: 我们大多数人不知道在我们去世后会发生什么，以及生命之后会发生什么。

sentences.en: And, you know, it can be a quite common thing as well.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，这也是一件相当普遍的事情。

sentences.en: Of course, some people experience it at some point, but we don't really talk about it very much.
sentences.zh: 当然，有些人会在某个时刻经历它，但我们其实很少谈论它。

sentences.en: So that's kind of where the research stemmed from.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是这项研究的起源。

sentences.en: Okay, so we're not necessarily thinking specifically about people who might have a palliative diagnosis or who think that they might not live as long as kind of people around them.
sentences.zh: 好的，所以我们不一定专门针对那些被诊断为姑息治疗或认为自己可能不会像周围人那样长寿的人。

sentences.en: We're thinking about the general kind of Dawson's Creek style existential ponderings of our own mortality.
sentences.zh: 我们考虑的是那种常规的、“恋爱时代”风格的、对我们自身死亡率的生存主义沉思。

sentences.en: Is that right?
sentences.zh: 是这样吗？

sentences.en: That's exactly right.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, it's the one thing in life that is inevitable to all of us.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是生活中对我们所有人来说都不可避免的一件事。

sentences.en: And that's exactly what the thesis focused on.
sentences.zh: 这正是本论文关注的焦点。

sentences.en: Okay, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 好的，完全同意。

sentences.en: Can you tell us a bit more about your thesis then and the terror management theory?
sentences.zh: 能给我们多讲讲你的论文以及恐怖管理理论吗？

sentences.en: What is that?
sentences.zh: 那是什么？

sentences.en: Yeah, of course.
sentences.zh: 好的，当然可以。

sentences.en: So terror management theory is a psychological theory that really tries to explain how we cope with the knowing that we will one day die.
sentences.zh: 恐怖管理理论是一个心理学理论，它真正试图解释我们如何应对“我们终有一天会死”这一认知。

sentences.en: And terror management theory states that because we're the only animal that's aware of their mortality, it's quite unique.
sentences.zh: 恐怖管理理论指出，因为我们是唯一意识到自己终将一死的动物，所以这是非常独特的。

sentences.en: And hence the term terror, because if we went through our life day to day, just thinking about the fact that, you know, we will want hasties to exist,
sentences.zh: 因此才有了“恐怖”这个词，如果我们日常生活中一直在思考这样一个事实，即我们终将不复存在，

sentences.en: that is quite terrifying to think about.
sentences.zh: 光是想想就会觉得非常可怕。

sentences.en: But the terror management theory states that basically we'll build up systems to buffer this terror or this fear, this death anxiety that we have.
sentences.zh: 但恐怖管理理论指出，基本上我们会建立系统来缓冲这种恐怖、这种恐惧，也就是我们拥有的死亡焦虑。

sentences.en: And we do this through systems like our culture, our personal values and relationships that act as buffers in a way.
sentences.zh: 我们通过诸如文化、个人价值观和人际关系等系统来做到这一点，它们在某种程度上起到了缓冲作用。

sentences.en: And these buffers give us a sense of meaning, they help us feel secure, so that the death anxiety doesn't overwhelm us.
sentences.zh: 这些缓冲带给我们一种意义感，它们帮助我们感到安全，这样死亡焦虑就不会压垮我们。

sentences.en: It's a bit like having an emotional toolkit for that death awareness.
sentences.zh: 这有点像是为这种死亡意识准备了一个情感工具包。

sentences.en: Okay, so terror management theory, TMT, is that something that's your own baby?
sentences.zh: 好的，那么恐怖管理理论，即TMT，这是你自己的原创成果吗？

sentences.en: Or is that already in the literature?
sentences.zh: 还是说它已经存在于相关文献中了？

sentences.en: Oh, no, that's been in the literature since I want to say like the 80s.
sentences.zh: 哦，不，我想说从20世纪80年代开始它就已经存在于文献中了。

sentences.en: It was three social psychologists who came up with this theory and it really started this idea of why do we need self-esteem?
sentences.zh: 是三位社会心理学家提出了这个理论，它真正开启了这样一个观念：为什么我们需要自尊？

sentences.en: And that's kind of what I've already touched upon in terms of these buffers.
sentences.zh: 这也就是我刚才在缓冲带方面已经提到过的内容。

sentences.en: So self-esteem help us buffer certain difficulties.
sentences.zh: 因此，自尊可以帮助我们缓冲某些困难。

sentences.en: And one of those difficulties is the awareness that we may one day die.
sentences.zh: 而这些困难之一就是意识到我们可能终有一天会死。

sentences.en: If we are living up to our worldviews or our values, then it gives us a sense of meaning that we are, you know, that life is worthwhile, that we are worthwhile people.
sentences.zh: 如果我们符合自己的世界观或价值观，它就会赋予我们一种意义感，即生活是值得过的，我们是有价值的人。

sentences.en: And that then buffers that with anxiety through self-esteem.
sentences.zh: 然后，它通过自尊来对冲这种焦虑。

sentences.en: Okay, so if things are going wrong and we have high kind of feelings about our own mortality,
sentences.zh: 好的，那么如果事情进展不顺利，并且我们对自己的死亡率产生了强烈的感受，

sentences.en: what might we be seeing in ourselves or perhaps in someone we care about or someone that we work with clinically?
sentences.zh: 我们在自己身上、或者在我们在乎的人身上、或者在我们的临床工作对象身上，可能会看到什么表现？

sentences.en: Well, I mean, I think a lot of us fear death anyway, because it's a big unknown.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我的意思是，我想我们很多人无论如何都害怕死亡，因为这是一个巨大的未知数。

sentences.en: Our brains try to keep us safe.
sentences.zh: 我们的大脑试图让我们保持安全。

sentences.en: It's a big don't get eaten machine, right?
sentences.zh: 它本质上是一台巨大的“别被吃掉”的机器，对吧？

sentences.en: So it's normal to have these thoughts pop into our mind or to have reminders day to day.
sentences.zh: 所以，这些想法突然闯入我们的脑海，或者日常生活中受到一些提醒，是很正常的。

sentences.en: You know, you may see a scene on TV or hear about someone's passing.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，你可能会在电视上看到一个场景，或者听到有人去世的消息。

sentences.en: And that does trigger these thoughts of mortality or reflection on life in ourselves.
sentences.zh: 这确实会激发我们对死亡的想法或对自己生命的沉思。

sentences.en: But normally we are pretty good at buffering those thoughts, like I said, through those mechanisMs.
sentences.zh: 但通常情况下，就像我说的，我们非常擅长通过那些机制来缓冲这些想法。

sentences.en: But for some people, they may have not had the opportunity to develop the buffers as well as others.
sentences.zh: 但对某些人来说，他们可能没有机会像其他人那样很好地发展出这些缓冲机制。

sentences.en: For example, this could be from, you know, things like early loss, trauma, insecure attachment styles,
sentences.zh: 例如，这可能是由于诸如早年丧亲、创伤、不安全型依恋风格等原因造成的，

sentences.en: kind of a lot of the things that we see in people who also develop mental health difficulties, you know, those early childhood adverse experiences.
sentences.zh: 这就像我们在那些同样出现心理健康困难的人身上看到的很多事情一样，也就是那些早年童年逆境经历。

sentences.en: And when we don't have those buffers or perhaps we manage our mortality in a way that's not productive or not helping us,
sentences.zh: 当我们没有这些缓冲，或者也许我们以一种没有成效或对我们没有帮助的方式来处理我们的死亡率时，

sentences.en: it can, or the literature at least, says that it can definitely lead to an increase in mental health difficulties.
sentences.zh: 它可能会——或者至少相关文献说，它绝对会导致心理健康困难的增加。

sentences.en: The research also states that death anxiety can be a transdiagnostic factor across different mental health disorders.
sentences.zh: 研究还表明，死亡焦虑可以成为各种心理健康障碍中共同的跨诊断因素。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And it is, it does crop up more than you might imagine.
sentences.zh: 而且它的确比你想象的更频繁地出现。

sentences.en: So I don't know if you've ever read any of the Hunger Games books, but I'm reading the new one at the moment, the one that was published in 2025.
sentences.zh: 所以，我不知道你是否读过任何《饥饿游戏》的书，但我现在正在读新的一本，也就是2025年出版的那本。

sentences.en: And it's focusing in on Haymitch, who in the first Hunger Games is Katniss's kind of mentor, but it's focusing in on his story when he was in the Hunger Games.
sentences.zh: 它聚焦于海米奇，在第一部《饥饿游戏》中他是凯妮丝的导师，但这本聚焦于他在参加《饥饿游戏》时的故事。

sentences.en: And it's interesting, one of the, one of the participants is kind of saying, actually, my hope is that I will die quickly and that my family won't have to watch this protracted,
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，其中一位参赛者说，实际上，我的希望是我能死得快一点，这样我的家人就不必看着这种旷日持久、

sentences.en: horrific death.
sentences.zh: 可怕的死亡。

sentences.en: And that's like, almost like hoping for that, that good death that we sometimes speak about.
sentences.zh: 这就好比近乎期盼着那种我们有时会谈论的“善终”。

sentences.en: But obviously in a, in a game show, a good death is perhaps different than, than the millionaire's death, which I think is spoken about,
sentences.zh: 但显然在游戏秀中，一个好的死亡可能不同于富人的死亡，我想人们谈到过的那种，

sentences.en: which is lying in a bed when you're a hundred, surrounded by people that you love.
sentences.zh: 也就是当你一百岁时躺在床上，周围都是你爱的人。

sentences.en: That's, that's kind of sometimes thought of as a millionaire's death.
sentences.zh: 这有时被认为是一种富人的死亡。

sentences.en: But, and then of course, Squid Games as well, like Squid Games is, you know, is around in our culture currently.
sentences.zh: 但是，当然还有《鱿鱼游戏》，比如《鱿鱼游戏》目前在我们的文化中也随处可见。

sentences.en: I've just literally finished season three yesterday, a bit disappointed actually.
sentences.zh: 我昨天刚刚看完第三季，其实稍微有点失望。

sentences.en: But it, yeah, like thinking about people's death and, and kind of whether that's quite a violent death or, or whether it's something actually that we hope we will live till our
sentences.zh: 但是，是的，比如思考人们的死亡，以及这究竟是一种相当暴力的死亡，还是说其实是我们希望自己能活到

sentences.en: older years.
sentences.zh: 老年。

sentences.en: We hope that we will, I guess, hit, hit some of those milestones that are different for each of us, but certainly, you know, for many people might include finding a life partner
sentences.zh: 我们希望自己能够，我猜，达成一些对每个人来说都不同的人生里程碑，但当然，对许多人来说可能包括找到终身伴侣，

sentences.en: or, you know, maybe having children or not having children or starting a business or, you know, making a success of your career, making yourself proud, making others proud.
sentences.zh: 或者也许生孩子或不生孩子，或者创业，或者在职业生涯中取得成功，让自己骄傲，让别人骄傲。

sentences.en: Like, you know, there's certain things that we might want to do.
sentences.zh: 就像，你知道的，有些特定的事情我们可能想做。

sentences.en: Some people, you know, might want to go on and become a grandparent or, you know, just like those self-imposed life goals.
sentences.zh: 有些人，你知道，可能想继续成为祖父母，或者，你知道，就像那些自我强加的生活目标。

sentences.en: And it's, is it, is it measuring ourselves up to how well we feel we have or haven't measured up to those goals that, that leads to us having this terror response?
sentences.zh: 那么，我们是否在用自己达到或未达到这些目标的程度来衡量自己，从而导致了这种恐怖反应？

sentences.en: Yeah, I think, I think you're absolutely right there.
sentences.zh: 是的，我想你说得绝对对。

sentences.en: So, um, what the research also states, and I think what you've started to describe here, we have different ways of dealing with our mortality.
sentences.zh: 所以，研究还表明，我想你刚才也开始描述了，我们有不同的方式来处理我们的死亡率。

sentences.en: And of course, we have different worldviews.
sentences.zh: 当然，我们有不同的世界观。

sentences.en: So, for example, if we take religion into account, of course, that kind of gives us a quite nice framework to work from and sets out, you know, if you do certain things, you
sentences.zh: 因此，举例来说，如果我们把宗教考虑在内，当然，这会给我们提供一个相当不错的框架来指导生活，并阐明，如果你做某些事情，

sentences.en: will have a good life, or perhaps you will go to heaven or be reincarnated after life.
sentences.zh: 你就会过上好日子，或者也许你会上天堂，或者在死后转世。

sentences.en: And then outside of religion, we can also think about these other ways of buffering other things, anxiety through what we call symbolic or literal immortality.
sentences.zh: 然后除了宗教之外，我们还可以考虑通过我们所谓的象征性或字面上的永生来缓冲其他事情、对冲焦虑的其他方式。

sentences.en: And what you've described there, having a life partner, having children, in a way that kind of buffers the death anxiety, because our legacy lives on.
sentences.zh: 而你刚才所描述的，拥有伴侣、拥有孩子，在某种程度上可以缓冲死亡焦虑，因为我们的精神得以延续。

sentences.en: So we can live on through our children, through our family.
sentences.zh: 所以我们可以通过我们的孩子、通过我们的家庭活下去。

sentences.en: So in a way that is a really nice buffer to have.

sentences.zh: 让我们激发更多的对话。

sentences.en: To quote Jack from
sentences.zh: 借用《泰坦尼克号》中杰克的话，

sentences.en: Titanic, let's make this count.
sentences.zh: 让我们不虚此行。

sentences.en: Psychologists, what if you could earn money beyond trading your time for money?
sentences.zh: 心理学家们，如果你们能赚取超越“出售时间换取金钱”的收入会怎么样？

sentences.en: I'm Dr. Marianne Trent, clinical psychologist, and I've been developing passive and recurring income streams since 2019.
sentences.zh: 我是临床心理学家玛丽安·特伦特博士（Dr. Marianne Trent），自 2019 年以来我一直在开发被动和循环收入流。

sentences.en: I have some exciting news.
sentences.zh: 我有一个激动人心的消息要宣布。

sentences.en: Sophie Foote's one-to-many program is now open for enrollment.
sentences.zh: 苏菲·富特（Sophie Foote）的一对多项目现在开放报名了。

sentences.en: It's designed to help you turn your expertise into scalable offers like courses, memberships, and digital products.
sentences.zh: 它旨在帮助你将专业知识转化为可规模化的产品，比如课程、会员制服务和数字产品。

sentences.en: I completed the program myself in 2022 and have since supported two cohorts of psychologists through their journeys too.
sentences.zh: 我在 2022 年亲自完成了这个项目，此后也一直支持两批心理学家走过他们的转化之旅。

sentences.en: And if you join through my affiliate link, you'll receive Sophie's bonuses, plus my own exclusive support package at no extra coSt. That includes six months of WhatsApp support,
sentences.zh: 如果你通过我的专属推广链接加入，你将获得苏菲提供的额外福利，以及我独家的全套支持，无需支付额外费用。这包括六个月的 WhatsApp 支持，

sentences.en: four group masterminds, masterclasses, personalized guidance, a Fortnum and Mason treat, and a time-limited one-to-one coaching bonus.
sentences.zh: 四场小组成头脑风暴会、大师班、个性化指导、一份福特南与梅森（Fortnum and Mason）的美食礼品，以及限时的一对一教练指导福利。

sentences.en: Enrollment closes on Monday the 16th of November at 10pm.
sentences.zh: 报名将于 11 月 16 日星期一晚上 10 点截止。

sentences.en: Find out more via my bonus page linked in the description.
sentences.zh: 通过简介中链接的我的专属福利页面了解更多信息。

sentences.en: And remember, you must purchase through my link to receive my bonuses.
sentences.zh: 请记住，你必须通过我的链接购买才能获得我的专属福利。

sentences.en: I'm here if you have any questions.
sentences.zh: 如果你有任何问题，我随时都在。
